content:
Date: Thursday, June 18, 2026

Selected Approach:
- Full build to the A/C — signals service + cold-launch snapshot

Approved implementation approach:
Build exactly what Andy decided. A new singleton FreedomStatsService owns the three fetches and the freedom-date/age/dollars-away math (preserved byte-for-byte from loadStatStrip()): toSignal(userProgress$) bridges progress, writable signals hold equity + birth-year, a computed() derives the stats plus a loading signal. The service is warm across navigation (instant re-entry) and persists a user-scoped snapshot of the displayed values to localStorage so cold launch paints real numbers immediately, then background-refreshes. My Profile saves auto-update it; FRED-196's KYC retry is preserved; the old loadStatStrip() machinery is deleted, not commented.

Andrew's Answers:
Q: Re-entry refresh policy. AC-3 says returning to tab3 shows the cached values instantly with "no second cold round of three fetches" (no dashes). Should the service silently background-refresh on re-entry (stale-while-revalidate — show cached instantly, refetch quietly, swap when fresh data returns) so equity stays current after an investment runs — or NOT refetch on re-entry at all until something explicitly changes (e.g. a My Profile save)? My recommendation: silent background refresh — instant cached paint, quiet revalidate, never a dash on re-entry. Required
  A (Andrew confirmed your prediction): Silent background refresh on re-entry — show cached instantly, revalidate quietly, swap when fresh data returns; never flash dashes on re-entry.
Q: Snapshot staleness cap. On cold launch the strip hydrates from the localStorage snapshot, then background-refreshes. Should the snapshot have a max age beyond which it's ignored (fall back to — instead of showing a stale number) — or always hydrate then immediately revalidate regardless of age? My recommendation: no hard TTL — always hydrate then refresh right away; a stale value is corrected within seconds, and offline a slightly-stale real number beats dashes. Optional
  A (Andrew confirmed your prediction): No hard TTL — always hydrate from the snapshot then immediately background-refresh; a stale value self-corrects in seconds and beats showing dashes offline.

Proceed with implementation.
